name: Arecibo Telescope
scope: Historical 305 m Arecibo Telescope after the Gregorian upgrade, with the spherical reflector, ground screen, three towers, cable anchorages and suspended receiver assembly as documented in 2006.

references.caption: Closeup of the feed antenna of the Arecibo Radio Telescope, at Arecibo, Puerto Rico.  The dish reflector of the telescope is built into a valley in the landscape, and the feed antenna is suspended by cables above it.  Since the reflector can't be moved, the telescope is steered to point at different regions of the sky by moving the feed antenna (in bell shaped dome) along on a curving track.  The dome shields the feed antenna from interfering radio signals.

originalReview.notes: Exact 2006 photograph confirms paired truss chords, diagonal steel bracing, ring tracks, the curved azimuth arm, protective geodesic Gregorian dome and the suspended line feed.

review.method: Exact published Qualla photograph and native creator public-domain release
review.notes: Reviewed Qualla first. Used the exact historical Arecibo exterior by photographer Alessandro Cai (OliverZena), who published it as his own work under a public-domain dedication. The other published images do not show this configuration or lack public-domain clearance.
